transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-27 15:00 PDT 
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jessie Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Avery Lee (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (HarborTrust Lead ML Eng), Mark Evans (Platform), Priya Rao (SRE), Tom Wu (QA)

Summary (auto): quick sync on latency tuning for the POC; Samir presented recent test runs; agreed on next steps for a 1k TTFT benchmark with streaming on dedicated pool; customer to send traces.

00:00 Jessie (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh just to set the agenda quick sync on latency numbers, Samir will share the run results and then we'll talk tuning and next steps
00:42 Samir (Redwood SE): yeah thanks jessie, um so quick context we re-ran the microbench with streaming enabled and smaller initial chunking, we saw TTFT drop about 120 to 180 ms depending on model variant, so that was promising, the rest of the tokens were roughly the same so total completion is similar but first byte noticeably faster
01:25 Lena (HarborTrust): sorry can you repeat the chunking part, like what do you mean by smaller initial chunking, is that the first-stream size?
01:40 Samir (Redwood SE): yeah exactly so instead of sending first token batch of like 64 tokens we forced the runtime to start streaming after the first 4-8 tokens to present partial output earlier, it's sort of the streaming window, and we also tuned kernel warmup to prioritize first token compute paths
02:10 Mark (Platform): okay so that sounds great for UX, but what about the increased request rate? if you start streaming earlier does that increase GPU overhead or overall qps cost?
02:35 Samir (Redwood SE): good question, there's a tradeoff — streaming can slightly increase per-request overhead due to more RPCs, but we offset that by shrinking the first chunk and enabling continuous KV cache so subsequent calls reuse the cache; in our dedicated runs overall GPU utilization actually improved because latency tail tightened and pipelines fed more consistently
03:05 Priya (SRE): can you remind me which hardware you ran on for those numbers? A100 or H100?
03:18 Samir (Redwood SE): these particular runs were on H100-nvlink, multi-instance with the new attention kernel; we also did A100 runs for parity and saw ~10-15% worse TTFT there, mostly due to kernel selection differences
03:50 Tom (QA): transcript mess, sometimes it says speaker 1 and 2 in the logs, ignore that, sorry.
04:05 Jessie (Redwood AE): no problem, audible logs are fine, um lena can you share current SLOs and seq len distributions again? we had the csv from last week but want to re-check the 95th distribution
04:25 Lena (HarborTrust): yeah I'll re-upload, but just to remind you our median seq is 64 tokens, 95th is about 420, 99th 1.2k, so the tail's long because of some batch extraction workflows
05:10 Samir (Redwood SE): that 95th at 420 explains why tuning for smaller chunk at first byte helps a lot for the majority, but we'll need different strategies for the 99th — e.g., dynamic truncation or chunked streaming plus early-stop heuristics
05:45 Mark (Platform): can we talk kernel selection — you mentioned custom attention kernel vs cuDNN, what's the impact there?
06:05 Samir (Redwood SE): sure, so cuDNN is stable and has broad performance but our newer custom kernels for the attention path can reduce token compute by ~20% at mid-seqs, the catch is memory pathing and compatibility: some quantized variants need bespoke kernels, and there are tradeoffs on latency jitter. For HarborTrust I'd recommend using the verified kernel set we tested on H100 first, then fall back to cuDNN on A100 or mixed GPU fleets
06:50 Lena (HarborTrust): do you have a doc that maps model quantization/profile to supported kernels? we ran into an issue where 4-bit quant broke a path last month
07:05 Samir (Redwood SE): yes, we'll share the kernel-selection notes, there's a matrix (we call it kernel-guide.pdf in the repo) that maps quantization->kernel->expected perf. we'll attach that after the call
07:28 Jessie (Redwood AE): also we'll include the short README about enabling streaming and adjusting first-chunk size in the SDK, that's been helpful for other banks that have strict tail SLOs
07:45 Lena (HarborTrust): perfect, thank you. quick question on batching: you recommended reducing batch size for TTFT but increase concurrency — can you explain the cost tradeoff again?
08:05 Samir (Redwood SE): yeah so per-token cost depends on how many tokens you amortize over a batch: larger batches are cheaper per token but hurt TTFT; increasing concurrency with smaller batches keeps throughput similar but can increase GPU memory pressure. On Dedicated you can provision more capacity or set autoscale burst to handle concurrency spikes — that's where Dedicated wins over hosted for predictable tail SLOs
08:40 Mark (Platform): is there an easy knob in the console to simulate request concurrency? we want to replay traces at different concurrency levels
08:52 Avery (CSM): yes in the Console there's a replay harness under the Route Diagnostics section, we can run your traces at configurable concurrency and sequence length buckets, Samir can help set that up
09:05 Samir (Redwood SE): I'll take that, we can also run the 1k-sample bench with the same harness and attach the raw logs so you can inspect token-level timings
09:25 Lena (HarborTrust): on the security side, we might need to do the on-prem pilot for higher volumes, given compliance. is Private deployment necessary to hit our cost targets or can we do Dedicated?
09:45 Jessie (Redwood AE): depends — Private gives you network isolation and control but upfront ops cost; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and consistent perf without you managing infra. For cost per token Dedicated usually wins unless you have capacity/utilization >70% and want to amortize ops overhead
10:10 Priya (SRE): also SSO/SAML and KMS integration questions — is audit logging the same across Dedicated and Private?
10:25 Jessie (Redwood AE): audit logs and KMS support are available for both, Private lets you hold keys in your HSM; Dedicated uses our KMS integration with customer-managed keys for encryption at rest and in transit, we'll send the security pack link
10:40 Tom (QA): minor note, the earlier benchmark had some transcription artifacts where 'KV cache' got transcribed as 'K-V cash' in the logs, just flagging in case you parse names
10:55 Samir (Redwood SE): noted; for the benchmark runs we keep a mapping file so parsers don't get confused. on the technical tweaks side, one more thing — we enabled prefix caching for repeated contexts and that dropped token compute for multi-turn flows by ~12% in our tests
11:20 Lena (HarborTrust): great — do you remember which workloads saw the KV cache wins? our multi-turn customer support threads should benefit a lot
11:35 Samir (Redwood SE): mainly chat-like multi-turn with repeating context, not so much single-shot extraction jobs. We'll include sample workload IDs in the benchmark.xlsx we upload
12:05 Mark (Platform): about the 99th tail — you mentioned dynamic truncation and early-stop, could that affect output quality? we can't lose regulatory-required fields in a response
12:30 Samir (Redwood SE): it can if applied naively, so we recommend quality-preserving heuristics: prioritize preserving labeled entities and required fields, or fall back to a longer path for critical requests. We'll show an example rule set in the tuning guide
13:05 Lena (HarborTrust): can you walk through the plan for the 1k TTFT run again? timeline and what you'll measure?
13:20 Samir (Redwood SE): yes, plan: use your provided traces (anonymized), split into median/95/99 buckets, run on the Dedicated H100 pool with streaming enabled and first-chunk sizes 4,8,16; measure TTFT, p50/95/99 latencies, token cost, and GPU utilization. We'll produce a summary and raw logs. Target to complete by 2026-11-03
14:05 Jessie (Redwood AE): perfect, and we'll follow-up with pricing and attach the security pack + kernel-guide.pdf + benchmark template
14:20 Lena (HarborTrust): thanks. one blocker — the legal team wants an explicit SLA for TTFT for the pilot, is that something Redwood provides for dedicated pilots?
14:38 Jessie (Redwood AE): we can provide a pilot SLA with SLO targets but enterprise-level contractual SLAs typically require Dedicated commitments; for pilots we do a best-effort target and operational runbook, but we can flag in the SOW what targets we'll aim for
14:58 Priya (SRE): okay please include that in the SOW draft, Priya will review it
15:10 Tom (QA): small QA note: we'll run smoke tests against streaming enabled and disabled to verify no regression in outputs due to partial streaming chunks
15:30 Samir (Redwood SE): good call, include QA smoke tests, we'll support that.
15:50 Jessie (Redwood AE): quick recap: Samir runs 1k TTFT with streaming on Dedicated H100, Lena shares traces and SLOs, Jessie sends pricing and security docs, schedule on-prem pilot for week of 11/10. Anything else?
16:15 Lena (HarborTrust): nope that's it thanks everyone
16:25 Jessie (Redwood AE): awesome thanks, we'll follow up over email with links.

References / links mentioned: benchmark.xlsx (will be uploaded to shared drive), kernel-guide.pdf (Redwood repo), security-pack.pdf (Redwood security docs), Console Route Diagnostics replay harness (link provided in follow-up)

Action items (auto): Samir to run benchmark and upload logs; Lena to provide traces; Jessie to send pricing/security docs.
